english.notes:
(i) Low Value shoplifting – either way offence - section 22A of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980 provides that 'low-value shoplifting' (value does not exceed £200) is an offence which is triable only summarily (see exceptions below). The cases of Candlish v Director of Public Prosecutions (2022) and Jobson v Director of Public Prosecutions (2025) confirm section 22A will be considered when the accused appears before the Magistrates Court to answer the charge; and that "until then, the offence of theft is, like all other offences of theft, an indictable offence, in that it is triable either way".
At the first appearance at the magistrates' court the value, aggregate value and ultimately mode of trial will be determined. Cases £200 and under will be treated as summary unless 22A(2) or (4) apply.
Otherwise, the effect of section 22A is that offences of low-value shoplifting cannot be sent to the Crown Court for trial or committed there for sentence; they will attract a maximum penalty of six months' custody; and they will be brought within the procedure in section 12 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980 that enables defendants in summary cases to be given the opportunity to plead guilty by post.
(ii) Time limit for prosecutions - Jobson v Director of Public Prosecutions (2025) has confirmed when charged, theft offences are indictable, and section 127(1) is disapplied by virtue of section 127(2). Where an offence is later deemed triable only summarily, it does not affect section 127 application and the offence remains an 'either way' offence with no time limit on prosecution.
Although the offence continues to be triable either-way and is not statute barred within 6 months, the aim of these changes was to speed up the process for courts when dealing with low value shoplifting cases. We would advise that every effort is made to prosecute these offences within the 6 month's otherwise the public interest test may not be satisfied and the courts will likely expect the delay to be justified. See additional notes on section 1(1).(iii) Where the value of the property stolen is under £100 the offence may be disposed of by the issue of a PND - PND Code DA12. Only ONE PND should ever be issued to an individual for retail theft. A PND should not be issued to an offender who is a substance mis-user. Where a PND is issued it should be recorded on PNC within 24 hours - according to ACPO guidelines.

other.penalty:
Either waySummary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 7 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Where the value of the property stolen is under £100-00p:- Penalty Notice for Disorder - £90-00p.

Note:
As from 08/04/2013 Penalty Notices for Disorder may ONLY be issued to offenders aged 18 years or over.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
